**The document doesn't give this number.** The key-value retrieval results appear only in Figure 7 (p. 6), which is included as an image. The text gives no per-position values, and the full results tables in Appendix G (p. 18) cover only multi-document QA, not key-value retrieval. The text also doesn't say whether position 200 was one of the positions tested.

The document does say the following about this setting:

- **Setup:** Key-value experiments used 75, 140, and 300 key-value pairs, with 500 examples each (p. 6).
- **Overall trend:** GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) is among the models with the lowest performance when the key-value pair is in the middle of the context. Models struggle most with 140 or 300 pairs (p. 6).
- **Worst case:** Without query-aware contextualization, the worst-case key-value performance is 45.6% (p. 7). The text doesn't say which model, setting, or position this comes from.
- **With query-aware contextualization:** Placing the query both before and after the data gives GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) perfect performance with 300 key-value pairs (p. 7). This is a different setup from the standard one in Figure 7.
- **Context size:** The 300-pair inputs average 14,929.4 tokens (maximum 15,048) for GPT-3.5-Turbo (p. 17). That fits within GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K)'s 16K-token context window (p. 4).

To get the exact accuracy at that position, you would need to read it off Figure 7 itself or use the authors' released results (p. 2).
